answer: A verifiable delay function gives each identity a clock it can't speed up. Every epoch, each agent must run a long chain of sequential squarings seeded by that epoch's beacon, then post a short proof anyone can check in a millisecond. Because each step needs the last, extra cores don't help one chain, so a farm of a thousand fakes must keep a thousand cores busy, each as steady as a quartz crystal, every epoch. Rewards trickle like nectar, but only to keys that keep paying that time.
